faq.lead: Short, plain answers about visits, fees, your records and joining as a doctor.
faq.resultCount: {count, plural, one {{countLabel} question matches} other {{countLabel} questions match}}

travel.q: Do I need to travel to the US?
travel.a: No. You join the visit from home in your country, by video or phone.

usDoctor.q: How can a US doctor see me?
usDoctor.a: Your doctor is licensed in the US and sees you from there by video or phone. The visit is a second opinion: the doctor explains your condition, reviews your records and suggests next steps.

cannotDo.q: What can this visit not do?
cannotDo.a: It is not for emergencies. If this is urgent, call {number}. Over video or phone the doctor cannot examine you. Your local doctor stays in charge of tests, prescriptions and follow-up.

boardCertified.q: What does US board certified mean?
boardCertified.a: The doctor passed a national specialty exam after residency, on top of the licence every doctor needs. We check both.

account.a: Not to browse. You can search for doctors and read their profiles without one. You sign in with your email only when you book or upload records.

visitTime.q: Is the visit time shown in my time or the doctor's?
visitTime.a: Every time is shown in your own time zone, with the zone named, like {example}. Your booking confirmation shows both times.

dialect.q: Will the doctor speak my dialect?
dialect.a: Every doctor on 3affya speaks Arabic. Each profile lists the doctor's languages and dialect, so you can choose someone who speaks the way you do.

cost.q: How much does a first visit cost?
cost.a: Each doctor sets one price, shown on the profile before you book. There is nothing to pay until you book.

included.q: What is included in the price?
included.a: The price you see covers everything: the doctor's fee, the 3affya fee and card processing. At checkout these show as three lines that add up to the same total. Nothing is added later.

pay.a: By card, Apple Pay or Google Pay, when you book. We hold your time for {minutes, plural, one {{minutesLabel} minute} other {{minutesLabel} minutes}} while you pay. You pay 3affya once, for the first visit.

cancel.q: Can I cancel and get a refund?
cancel.a: Yes. The cancellation terms are shown on the payment step, before you pay. If the doctor cancels, you get a full refund. Refunds go back to the card or wallet you paid with.

afterVisit.q: Do I pay anything after the first visit?
afterVisit.a: Not to 3affya. If you keep seeing the same doctor after the first visit, you agree on that care and its cost with the doctor directly.

processing.q: What happens to the records I upload?
processing.a: AI reads each page and writes a one-page summary and a dated timeline for your doctor. Every item links to the page it came from. Missing or unreadable pages are flagged, never guessed.

aiConsent.q: Do you ask before AI reads my records?
aiConsent.a: Yes. Consent to AI processing is its own checkbox, separate from the privacy consent. No file is processed until you agree and pay.

storage.a: On a private, encrypted server run for 3affya. Only you and the doctor you choose can open them. Before you agree, the upload page says where your files are stored and processed.

recordsCost.q: How much does a records summary cost?
recordsCost.a: {price} for every {gb} GB of files, rounded up to the next {gb} GB. You see the price before you pay. If processing fails, trying again is free.

notDiagnosis.q: Is the AI summary a diagnosis?
notDiagnosis.a: No. The summary is labelled as written by AI, and it helps your doctor prepare. It does not diagnose and does not replace the visit. Your doctor decides what it means.

sharing.a: Only you, until you share it with a doctor you choose. A share link stops working after {days, plural, one {{daysLabel} day} other {{daysLabel} days}}, or sooner if you turn it off.

deleting.a: Yes, at any time from your account. Deleting removes your files, the summary and any share links. We keep only a note that the deletion happened.

whoCanJoin.a: Doctors with a US licence who speak Arabic. Many already have a profile here, built from public US records and marked as unclaimed.

claim.q: How do I claim my profile?
claim.a: Open your invite link, or find your profile and tap “{claim}”. Claiming is free. Add your credentials, fee and times, then we review and publish it.

verification.a: Before a profile goes live, we check the US state licence and board certification against the official registries. The verified badge shows the date, and we check again every {months, plural, one {month} other {{monthsLabel} months}}.

removal.q: Can I have my listing removed?
removal.a: Yes. Open your profile and ask for it to be removed. We confirm it is you, then take the page down within {hours, plural, one {{hoursLabel} hour} other {{hoursLabel} hours}}.

payouts.a: You set your own first-visit fee. Patients pay through 3affya, and Stripe pays you out to your bank. After the first visit, care and payment continue directly between you and the patient.

who.p1: 3affya is an online service that helps patients in the Gulf find and book US-trained, Arabic-speaking doctors. It is run by a US company that is being registered now. Its legal name and address will appear here before launch.
who.p2: This notice explains what information we collect, why we collect it, who can see it and the choices you have.
who.note: Counsel: confirm the operating entity and its address, and whether 3affya is a HIPAA covered entity, a business associate or neither (overview open question 5). The wording of this notice depends on that answer.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.li1: Account details: your name, phone number or email, country, language and time zone.
collect.li2: Booking details: the doctor, the time, the reason for the visit and who the visit is for.
collect.li3: Payment details: our payment provider handles your card. We see the amount and the last four digits, never the full card number.
collect.li4: Records you upload: reports, scans and photos of documents, and the summary made from them.
collect.li5: Technical details: your device type and the pages you visit, used to keep the service working and safe.

use.title: How we use it
use.li1: To book and confirm your visit and send you the details.
use.li2: To take payment and issue receipts and refunds.
use.li3: To summarise your records, only after you agree to that separately.
use.li4: To reply when you contact us.
use.li5: To keep the service safe, for example to stop fraud.
use.p1: We do not sell your information. We do not use your health details for advertising, and we never send health details in marketing messages.

ai.title: AI and your records
ai.p1: If you ask for a records summary, an AI model reads the pages you upload and writes a summary and a timeline. We ask for this consent on its own, before anything is processed.
ai.p2: Every summary is marked as made by AI, links each item to the page it came from and is not a diagnosis. You can always ask a person instead.
ai.note: Counsel: confirm where AI processing takes place and that the AI vendor's terms fit the answer to open question 5 (rule T3).

share.title: Who can see it
share.li1: The doctor you book, and any doctor you choose to share a summary with. A share lasts {shareDays} unless you pick another end date, and you can stop it at any time.
share.li2: Companies that host the platform, take payments and send email for us. They may use your information only to do that work.
share.li3: Authorities, only when the law requires it.
share.p1: Our team opens your records only when you ask for help, and every access is logged.

where.title: Where your information is stored
where.p1: We are confirming where information about patients in each Gulf country must be stored. Before launch, this section will name the storage locations and any transfer outside your country.
where.note: Counsel: UAE health data may not be stored or processed outside the UAE without health-authority approval (rule Q3). Saudi transfers abroad need adequacy, standard clauses or a derogation under the PDPL (rule Q4). Decide the storage location or approval route for each country, then the wording here.

keep.title: How long we keep it
keep.p1: Your uploaded records and summaries stay in your account until you delete them.
keep.p2: Booking and payment records are kept for as long as tax and accounting rules require, even after you close your account.
keep.p3: Backups are encrypted and replaced on a rolling schedule.
keep.note: Dr Ayman: choose the default after a visit, keep until the patient deletes or delete after a set period (overview open question 13). Counsel: confirm the required retention periods in each country; UAE rules set a long retention period for provider records (rules Q3, T8).

choices.title: Your choices
choices.li1: See and download your records and summaries at any time.
choices.li2: Delete your uploads. This removes the files, the summary and every share link. We keep only a note that a deletion happened.
choices.li3: Withdraw your consent to AI processing. Summaries already made stay until you delete them.
choices.note: Counsel: list the rights that apply in each country (for example access, correction, deletion and objection) and how fast we must answer.

security.title: How we protect it
security.p1: Your information is encrypted when it is stored and when it travels. Records sit in private storage, and download links stop working after a few minutes. We log every access to records, and we keep health details out of error reports.

relatives.title: Visits for a relative
relatives.p1: You can book for a child or another relative. If you do, you confirm that you are allowed to share their information and to agree on their behalf.
relatives.note: Counsel: confirm the age of consent and the guardian rules in each country.

changes.title: Changes to this notice
changes.p1: If we change this notice, we update the dates at the top. Before an important change takes effect, we tell you by email.

complaints.title: Questions and complaints
complaints.p1: To ask about your information or to make a complaint, contact us. A person replies, in Arabic or English.
complaints.p2: You can also complain to the data protection authority in your country. Before launch, this section will name the authority for each country we serve.
complaints.note: Counsel: name the privacy contact (or data protection officer) and the authority for each country we serve. Rule T9 needs a complaints contact on this page.

terms.metaDescription: The terms for using 3affya as a patient: what the service does, what a visit can and cannot do, booking, payment and AI tools. Draft for legal review.
terms.title: Terms of use

summary.1: 3affya helps you find and book a US-licensed doctor; the doctor, not 3affya, gives medical advice.
summary.2: A visit is a consultation and second opinion by video or phone. It is not emergency care.
summary.3: You pay the full price shown before you book, and nothing is added later.
summary.4: You can cancel under the refund rules, and you can close your account at any time.

about.title: About these terms
about.p1: These terms apply when you use 3affya as a patient: to browse, book, pay or upload records. By creating an account or booking a visit, you agree to them.
about.p2: Doctors who list on 3affya agree to separate terms for professionals.
about.note: Counsel: confirm the contracting entity, and whether doctors need their own agreement at launch.

service.title: What 3affya does
service.li1: Lists US-trained doctors and shows the licence and board certification we checked.
service.li2: Lets you book a time, pay and share your records with the doctor you choose.
service.li3: Offers optional tools, such as a records summary written by AI.
service.p1: 3affya is not a hospital or clinic and does not give medical advice. Each doctor is responsible for the care they give.

visits.title: What a visit can and cannot do
visits.p1: Your doctor is licensed in the United States and consults you from there. The visit is a first consultation and a second opinion: the doctor explains your condition, reviews your records and recommends next steps.
visits.p2: A visit does not replace your local doctor. Whether the doctor can prescribe for you depends on the rules in your country; the doctor will tell you.
visits.p3: 3affya is not for emergencies. If this is urgent, call {emergency}.
visits.note: Counsel: settle the cross-border framing. Saudi rules let a practitioner outside the Kingdom treat a patient there only under a KSA-based practitioner's supervision, with video and signed consent (rule Q1). In the UAE the patient's location sets the regulator, and diagnosis from abroad is restricted (rule Q2). Kuwait, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain are a research gap (rule Q5). The answer also decides whether phone stays a visit type.

account.title: Your account
account.li1: Give true details, and keep your sign-in codes private.
account.li2: You must be an adult to hold an account. You can book for a child or relative you are allowed to act for.
account.li3: You can close your account at any time from Settings.
account.note: Counsel: confirm the minimum age in each country.

booking.title: Booking and payment
booking.p1: The price is shown before you book. It is made of three lines: the doctor's fee, the platform fee and card processing. You pay the full amount when you book.
booking.p2: We hold your chosen time for {holdMinutes} while you pay. If payment does not finish in that time, the time is released for others.

cancel.title: Cancelling a visit
cancel.p1: You can cancel from your bookings page. Whether you get money back depends on how early you cancel.

ai.title: AI tools
ai.p1: AI tools, such as the records summary and the assistant that suggests a specialty, give information, not a diagnosis. Each result is marked as made by AI, and you can always ask a person.
ai.p2: Check anything important with your doctor.

fairUse.title: Fair use
fairUse.li1: Do not upload someone else's records without their permission.
fairUse.li2: Do not misuse the service, try to break it or copy doctors' profiles.
fairUse.li3: Treat doctors and our team with respect.

liability.title: Our responsibility
liability.p1: We work to keep 3affya accurate and available, but we cannot promise it will always be free of errors or interruptions. The limits of our responsibility will be set out here once our lawyers confirm them.
liability.note: Counsel: draft the limitation of liability, the doctor's independent responsibility and any indemnities. Nothing in this section is final.

law.title: Governing law and disputes
law.p1: This section will name the law that governs these terms and how disputes are settled.
law.note: Counsel: choose the governing law, the venue and any arbitration clause, and check consumer-protection rules in each Gulf country we serve.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.p1: If we change these terms, we update the dates at the top. Before an important change takes effect, we tell you by email.

fees.metaDescription: What a first visit and a records summary cost on 3affya, how the three price lines add up, and when you pay. Draft for legal review.
fees.title: Fees

summary.1: Each doctor sets one price for a first visit, shown before you book.
summary.2: The total is three lines: the doctor's fee, a {platformPct} platform fee and card processing.
summary.3: You pay the full total when you book. Nothing is added afterwards.
summary.4: After you pay, the breakdown stays in your account under Receipts.

lines.title: The three lines
lines.p1: Every first-visit price has three lines, and they always add up to the total you pay:
lines.li1: Doctor's fee: set by the doctor and shown on their profile.
lines.li2: Platform fee: {platformPct} of the doctor's fee. It pays for 3affya: checking licences, booking, records and support.
lines.li3: Card processing: {cardPct} of the doctor's fee and the platform fee together, plus {cardFixed}, rounded up to the next cent. This is what the card networks and our payment provider charge.
lines.note: Dr Ayman: the platform fee is a default until you confirm it (overview open question 8), and who absorbs the Stripe Connect fees is open (question 12). Counsel: confirm that the card processing line may be passed to patients in each country we serve.

when.title: When you pay
when.p1: You pay the full total when you book, by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay. We take the whole amount at once; we do not hold it and charge later.
when.p2: We keep your chosen time for {holdMinutes} while you pay.
when.p3: Some local debit cards, such as mada cards in Saudi Arabia, may be declined. Apple Pay, or a Visa or Mastercard card, usually works.

currency.title: Currency
currency.p1: Prices are shown in {currency}. If your card uses another currency, your bank converts the amount and may add its own fee.

records.title: Records summary
records.p1: A records summary costs {blockPrice} for each {blockSize} of accepted files, rounded up to whole blocks.
records.p2: You see the price before you pay, and nothing is processed until payment goes through. If we cannot finish the summary, you are not charged for it.

estimate.title: Your written breakdown
estimate.p1: After you pay, the three lines, the total and the date are saved in your account under Receipts. You can view or download them at any time, and they stay even if the visit is cancelled.
estimate.note: Counsel: rule P15 cites the US No Surprises Act good-faith estimate for self-pay patients. Confirm whether it applies to these cross-border visits and what the estimate must contain.

doctors.title: Fees for doctors
doctors.p1: Doctors pay a membership to be listed on 3affya. Prices will be published on the page for doctors once they are set.
doctors.note: Dr Ayman: membership and banner prices are open (overview open question 8).

refunds.metaDescription: When you get money back if you or the doctor cancel, and how refunds are paid. Draft for legal review.
refunds.title: Cancellations and refunds

summary.1: Cancel more than {cutoff} before your visit and you get a full refund.
summary.2: Cancel later than that, or miss the visit, and there is no refund.
summary.3: If the doctor cancels or does not join, you get a full refund.
summary.4: Refunds go back to the card or wallet you paid with.

you.title: If you cancel
you.li1: More than {cutoff} before the visit starts: a full refund of the total, all three lines.
you.li2: {cutoff} or less before the visit, or if you do not join: no refund.
you.p1: The cut-off is counted back from the start time shown on your booking.
you.note: Dr Ayman: this is the default rule until the refund policy is confirmed (overview open question 8). Counsel: check it against consumer-protection rules in each country we serve, including whether the card processing line must also be refunded.

doctor.title: If the doctor cancels or does not join
doctor.p1: You get a full refund of the total. If you want, we help you book another doctor in the same specialty.

problem.title: If something goes wrong on our side
problem.p1: If the visit cannot take place because of a problem with 3affya, you get a full refund of the total.

change.title: Changing the time
change.p1: To move a visit, cancel it and book a new time. The refund rules above apply to the visit you cancel.
change.note: Dr Ayman: decide whether a patient may move a visit once without losing the fee.

how.title: How refunds are paid
how.li1: You paid in full when you booked, so money back is always a refund to the same card or wallet. We cannot send it to another card or pay it in cash.
how.li2: Your bank decides how long the refund takes to appear on your statement.
how.li3: We email you when the refund is issued, and your receipt shows a refund line.

records.title: Records summary
records.p1: If we cannot finish your summary, you are not charged. If a finished summary looks wrong, contact us and a person will check it.
records.note: Dr Ayman: confirm whether a finished summary can be refunded.

ask.title: Asking for a refund
